bundles.title: Governor: adaptive slot control and free-memory gate
bundles.description_excerpt:
Improve the board slot governor that LMW-4 installed (PR #72 and its fix; log at ~/.multica-codex/board-governor.jsonl). Keep it small and extend the existing governor; do not add a second one.

1. Adaptive limit (AIMD, as in Netflix concurrency-limits): grow the slot count by one at a time only after a sustained healthy window (load per core, memory pressure, swap and compressor growth, board response time all good), and cut it multiplicatively on pressure (for example halve on high disk wait or memory pressure, to zero on emergency). Replace fixed thresholds where they cause the limit to stick, such as the current hold at 7 with reason pressure_or_reserve while load is around 8 on 14 cores.
2. Start gate (as in GNU parallel --memfree and make -l): before the board starts a new agent, require free memory above a floor plus the per-agent cost (about 2 GB and 0.8 cores from the live readings), and load below a ceiling; otherwise the task stays queued.
3. Waiting agents: make the explicit-wait path the default for long waits (waiting on another task, a PR merge, a deploy window, a reset), so waiting agents release their slot. Document how an agent should wait in the wiki how-to and worker instructions.
4. Read the AGPL-free ideas only; do not copy code from Netflix concurrency-limits or other projects.

Prove it on the live board: a log excerpt showing the limit rising one slot at a time after a healthy window, falling on a real or simulated pressure spike, a start held back by the memory gate, and a waiting agent releasing its slot so a queued task starts. Install without interrupting running agent sessions.

bundles.title: Make the SRW release gate fast and run it once per commit
bundles.description_excerpt:
Verification is the SRW bottleneck (Shyam, 2026-10-28: 'why is verification taking so long'). Facts from 2026-10-27/28: one full run of test_srw16_release_gate.js took 1303 s (about 22 min) on SRW-68; each task runs it several times (the agent's own run, the board check, again after every review round, again after every rebase when another task merges, and again in the deploy task); heavy runs 2 to 4 jobs at a time, and today it curtailed SRW jobs 15 times and paused them 9 times on load.

Goal: a task's gate costs minutes, not an hour, without weakening what it checks.
1. Profile the gate: time per step (index-lotto, copy-trading, real-corpus, reject-all, feature gate, and the rest) over three runs; find what dominates and why (serial replay, repeated setup, cold dependency installs, sleeps or polling).
2. Speed it up: parallelise independent steps inside one heavy admission within the CPU budget heavy grants, reuse setup, and keep the full real-post corpus replay. Consider 5 variations and pick by measured time.
3. Run once per commit: write a gate receipt keyed by the commit SHA (and Node version and lockfile hash); the board check, the reviewer and the deploy automation reuse a passing receipt for the same SHA instead of rerunning. Any change to the commit means a new run.
4. Keep every existing assertion; a deliberately broken commit must still fail.
Proof: before and after timings for each step and in total (target: total under 8 minutes on this Mac under heavy), a negative control that still fails, the board check reusing a receipt for an unchanged SHA, and the gate passing through ~/.local/bin/heavy. This task is the only one allowed to change test_srw16_release_gate.js and its runner; other tasks keep running it unchanged.

bundles.title: Misread tracking and learning loop for THALA parses
bundles.description_excerpt:
With timed-only mode off (2026-10-28), the paper bot acts on loosely written human-desk posts. Misreads are acceptable on paper, but they must be measured and driven down.

Build on the existing owners: the SRW-55 nightly classifier learning loop (clef_nightly_learning.js, clef_nightly_labeller.js, clef_nightly_replay.js) and the posts audit the daily check produces. No parallel pipeline.

1. Misread ledger: for every post the bot acted on or refused, record what it parsed (symbol, contract, side, size, trigger) and the ground truth, taken from THALA's later posts in the same thread (fills, trims, 'I bought', corrections), the actual contract traded, and the Telegram/Discord reply history. Classify each as correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call, or unclear.
2. Daily misread rate per category and per channel (Telegram, each Discord alert channel), with the worst examples, in the daily check report.
3. Learning: confirmed misreads become labelled examples for the nightly loop, and the nightly replay must show the rate falling or holding on the last 30 days before any parser change is promoted (the loop's existing promotion gate).
4. Guard: a misread class that repeats three times in a day raises an operator alert with the examples, without stopping trading.

Check 4 theories when a misread class appears, and consider 5 variations for the ground-truth matching rule. Proof: run the ledger on the stored posts since 2026-10-20 and today's live posts, show the per-category rate and 10 labelled examples, and show one nightly replay using them. Paper only; never print secrets; use heavy for heavy commands.
